claims.text: Microcompression testing of microscale pillars combined with in-situ SEM imaging can reveal deformation mechanisms in FeNiCrMn HEA.
The deformation mechanisms revealed by microscale testing contribute to the mechanical strength of FeNiCrMn HEA.
These deformation mechanisms have been overlooked in bulk-testing studies.
Conventional casting followed by annealing ensures a homogeneous, single-phase FeNiCrMn microstructure.
Focused ion beam milling can be used to fabricate FeNiCrMn micropillars for microcompression testing.
Local grain-boundary configurations mediate plastic deformation in FeNiCrMn HEA.
Dislocation-nucleation sites mediate plastic deformation in FeNiCrMn HEA.
Compressive stress in microscale FeNiCrMn samples activates discrete dislocation events.
Compressive stress in microscale FeNiCrMn samples produces strain localization along grain boundaries.
In-situ SEM imaging enables direct observation of deformation mechanisms that are less accessible in bulk tests.
Discrete dislocation events and grain-boundary strain localization govern the mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn HEA.
Microcompression will produce stepwise load drops associated with sudden dislocation motion or grain-boundary sliding.
The observed deformation events will lead to measurable strain-hardening effects.
Microscale deformation signatures will provide clearer insight into strengthening mechanisms than standard bulk tests.
Traditional bulk mechanical tests provide average stress-strain behavior without high-resolution information about local deformation.
Deformation observations made in micropillars may be scale-dependent and may not fully represent bulk behavior.
FIB-induced damage may affect the measured deformation behavior.
Load-displacement data can be correlated with in-situ SEM images to identify localized deformation events.
